transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Bennett (Lyra - Head of Strategic Alliances), Priya Shah (Lyra - GTM Lead), Ahmed Rahman (Lyra - Channel Ops)

Summary:
Quick partner co-sell / pipeline review. Lyra shared top joint opportunities and timeline; discussed how to structure partner margin, proof-of-value benchmarks, and legal/procurement cadence. SE details on pilot env, expected latency/cost tradeoffs, and dedicated vs hosted recommendations. Agreed next steps: pricing spreadsheet, benchmark plan, joint exec intro, security docs share.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we have about 45 minutes. I'll kick off — Jordan from Redwood, AE. Maya will cover technical bits. Tom, Priya, Ahmed, thanks for carving out time.
[00:22] Tom: Yeah thanks Jordan. Quick agenda from our side, we want to run through the pipeline, prioritization for joint outreach, and, uh, understand the pilot options.
[00:35] Priya: Yep, also want to confirm margins for partner-sourced deals and what kind of co-sell motion we can tell our reps.
[00:42] Jordan: Totally. Maya, quick intro?
[00:45] Maya: Hi all, Maya Patel, solutions engineer at Redwood; I'll go over the pilot architecture and the performance expectations — and then we can talk about the benchmarking plan.
[00:55] Ahmed: Sounds good. For context, Lyra has a handful of prospects where they want an LLM inference partner for e-comm personalization and a couple of regulated finance leads. So the security stuff is a big deal.
[01:08] Jordan: Right, and I've already pulled the SOC2 appendix and notes on private deployments, we'll share those.
[01:15] Tom: Great. Okay to the pipeline, I'll open screen - I'll just list the top six: RetailCo (e-comm personalization), FinSecure (regulated finance), Mediva (healthcare triage), AdFactory (ad creative at scale), BankNorth (large bank - POC required), and SparkOps (platform partner). RetailCo and FinSecure are highest priority.
[01:36] Priya: RetailCo is looking to push a pilot in April, wants 1-2 week proof of value, sub-100ms 1k token latency target for chat recommender.
[01:46] Maya: Sub-100ms at 1k tokens is challenging on hosted multi-tenant, depends on model and batching, but with dedicated pools or optimized quantized variants we can often get under 150ms in our tests. There might be variability, especially at tails.
[02:06] Tom: Hmm, ok. They said OpenAI latency is good today but cost is high; we want to show comparable latency and better unit economics.
[02:14] Jordan: Right, so the two levers are routing + dedicated capacity. For RetailCo we could propose Redwood Dedicated with a smaller reserved pool to meet latency SLOs and then suggest burst to hosted for spikes.
[02:27] Ahmed: And from Lyra's side, what's the typical commit level for RetailCo-sized pilots? They expect budget constraints.
[02:36] Maya: For pilots we often run a 2-4 week dedicated trial on a smaller GPU set, or we can stand up a private tenant in the customer's VPC if they need isolation. Costs are typically absorbed as credit during POC but we can structure a short-term reserved capacity with a trial discount.
[02:54] Priya: Ok, that helps. For FinSecure / BankNorth those will need private deployment and KMS/HSM integration. Any rough timeline?
[03:04] Maya: Private deployment can take 4-8 weeks depending on network and compliance requirements. KMS integration adds a bit of time but we've done a handful of bank pilots; we have a checklist. We'll share the security brief.
[03:17] Tom: Can you confirm log retention and audit log granularity — our customers will ask.
[03:22] Jordan: Yes we have per-request audit logs, retention is configurable; for enterprise we push to customer's SIEM or S3. I'll share the SOC2 specifics and the docs.
[03:34] [crosstalk] Priya: And SSO?
[03:36] Maya: SSO via SAML is supported, RBAC is granular.
[03:40] Jordan: Okay moving on to co-sell economics — Lyra asked about partner cuts and referral vs co-sell.
[03:47] Tom: We typically prefer co-sell where Lyra reps take credit and we split commission, but we want clarity on uplift and margin math.
[03:55] Jordan: We have a standard partner pricing spreadsheet — shows list price, partner uplift, reseller discount tiers. I'll send that after the call. For deals where Lyra leads, typical co-sell uplift is 12-18% depending on volume and net-new. We'll model examples for RetailCo.
[04:12] Priya: Can you show an example P&L for a 100k ARR deal?
[04:18] Jordan: Yeah we'll run a sample in the spreadsheet.
[04:21] Maya: Back on tech — for the RetailCo pilot to meet latency they should commit to a dedicated pool and use a quantized 8-bit variant. That reduces cost and improves throughput. But note: quantization may slightly affect generation quality on edge cases; we'll run evals with their prompt set.
[04:39] Tom: Is that something you can quantify? Like quality delta?
[04:42] Maya: We usually run side-by-side evals on our eval harness against their prompt sets; often delta is <3% on top-line metrics but depends. We'll include the eval results in the benchmark report.
[04:53] Ahmed: For procurement, Lyra asks if Redwood accepts standard Lyra PO terms? The legal team wants a playbook.
[05:01] Jordan: We can start with a Statement of Work and pilot addendum. For enterprise contracts we engage legal but we try to keep pilot terms light. Ahmed, if you send a redline template we'll have legal look within 5 business days.
[05:13] Ahmed: Okay will send the template.
[05:18] [60s timestamp approx omitted] Jordan: Next, technical checklist for the benchmark — Maya, could you run through steps?
[05:22] Maya: Sure. Step 1: define target scenarios and sample prompt set (RetailCo will provide). Step 2: decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Step 3: configure model variant and quantization profile. Step 4: run throughput & latency benchmarks with our harness, record token costs. Step 5: evaluate quality with their prompts. We aim to produce a one-pager with latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
[05:48] Priya: For step 2, RetailCo prefers not to do private in pilot; they'd like hosted or dedicated.
[05:54] Maya: Hosted multi-tenant tends to be cheaper but less deterministic on latency; dedicated is more predictable. We can also configure smart routing to keep costs down but still hit latency SLOs.
[06:05] Tom: Does Redwood support prefix caching / KV cache on our workloads — many of our prompts reuse context.
[06:11] Maya: Yes, we have KV cache and prefix caching. I'll probably say KV cache but I sometimes hear it as K-V cash on calls — sorry the transcript sometimes mangles that. But yes, prefix caching helps for repeated context and reduces tokens served.
[06:26] Priya: Ok good. On the topic of metrics, can Redwood break down token costs at the route level? Our reps want per-route cost so they can justify pricing to customers.
[06:36] Jordan: Yes Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. We can share a sample dashboard.
[06:42] Ahmed: Any known limitations with model catalog? They asked about custom fine-tuned models.
[06:47] Maya: We support hosting customer fine-tuned weights and model variants; for private deployments it's straightforward, for hosted we'd want to validate size and performance profiles. There are some kernel selection constraints for very large custom layers but we can work through that.
[07:04] Tom: Great. Switching back to GTM — Priya, what's Lyra's timeline for joint outreach?
[07:09] Priya: We want to start joint emails and AE intro calls the week of April 6. We want a 2-week lead time to prepare materials and train reps.
[07:18] Jordan: So we should have pricing, target use-case one-pager, and benchmark plan by March 30. Does that work?
[07:25] Priya: Yes.
[07:27] Jordan: And we'll do a joint deck for RetailCo with customized ROI numbers.
[07:31] Tom: Also want a co-sell playbook doc for Lyra reps: qualification, objection handling (latency/cost), and who to loop in on procurement.
[07:40] Jordan: We'll draft that — Maya and I will produce a 2-3 slide playbook.
[07:45] [small pause, typing audible] Maya: I have a question on benchmarking environment — for accurate latency numbers we should run tests from the target region. RetailCo is on us-east-1 for infra; we can stand up test instances there.
[07:58] Priya: Confirmed, RetailCo's pilot will run in us-east-1.
[08:02] Maya: Cool, we'll provision the test tenant there.
[08:06] Tom: On the procurement cadence, can we include a short-term reserved commitment that is refundable or creditable if they convert to full contract? Customers prefer not to pre-pay.
[08:16] Jordan: We can structure trial credits or a short-term reserved with credit toward the first 6 months if they convert; I'll outline options in the pricing spreadsheet.
[08:26] Ahmed: Legal will want to see data residency guarantees for BankNorth and FinSecure.
[08:31] Maya: For private deployments we can guarantee data stays within the customer's VPC/region. For hosted we have region controls and contracts that specify residency.
[08:40] Tom: Any red flags or blockers from Redwood side for these six prospects?
[08:45] Maya: Not major. For BankNorth and FinSecure the timeline is driven by legal and KMS integration; for RetailCo it's mostly latency/cost tradeoffs. We'll surface any kernel-level model compatibility if custom models arise.
[08:59] Priya: Good. For the joint outreach, what's the preferred intro template? Internal one or a Redwood-Lyra co-branded?
[09:05] Jordan: Co-branded is better. We'll send an example template.
[09:09] Tom: Ok. Quick question — who owns the SSO/identity connector during pilot? Lyra or RetailCo?
[09:15] Maya: For pilots it's often Lyra-managed for co-sell demos; if RetailCo wants to own production SSO we handoff during onboarding.
[09:23] [minor laughter] Priya: Makes sense.
[09:26] Jordan: Alright, recap of agreed next steps: Jordan to send partner pricing spreadsheet & SOC2 appendix; Maya to draft benchmark plan and test checklist; Tom to share top-6 prospect contact list; Ahmed to confirm procurement timing/PO process. We'll aim to have materials ready by March 30 and schedule the joint exec intro week of March 8.
[09:50] Tom: Quick nit — can Redwood provide a short ROI calc that includes cost per 1M tokens and projected savings vs OpenAI for the same throughput?
[09:58] Maya: Yes we'll include cost per million tokens and sample savings scenarios using their conversation volumes.
[10:04] Priya: Great. Anything else?
[10:07] Ahmed: One more from legal — are there ever export control or model IP concerns when hosting customer fine-tunes?
[10:13] Jordan: We have standard terms; we can discuss specifics after we see the fine-tune artifacts. If anything unusual arises legal will notify.
[10:22] Priya: Alright thanks everyone.
[10:25] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the doc bundle.
[10:29] Tom: Appreciate it, talk soon.

End of transcript.
